parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files cover one concern: X-ray rules that judge account-cluster risk from PortfolioDetails['accounts']. Each extends the shared Rule base class the same way. Each passes ExchangeRateDataService to super, builds its key from its class name, and gets the language code through getLanguageCode() and its settings key through getKey(). Each implements the same set of methods (evaluate, getConfiguration, getName, getSettings), and both translate messages the same way, through i18nService.getTranslation with ids under 'rule.accountClusterRisk*'. Neither file works around the Rule abstraction. Each file owns its own rule logic: the largest-account investment-ratio threshold lives only in current-investment.ts, and the single-account count check lives only in single-account.ts. Some boilerplate repeats: both return false with a '.false.invalid' message when there are no accounts, and both default isActive to true. That is the per-rule pattern the Rule contract asks for, not a shared invariant copied out of its proper home.
